title: Learning to Decode Quantum LDPC Codes via Cluster-Based Sequential Belief Propagation
authors: Mohsen Moradi, Taejoon Kim, Rémi A. Chou, David G. M. Mitchell
abstract: Belief-propagation (BP) decoding for quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) codes is attractive due to its low complexity, but its performance is often limited by short cycles, degeneracy, and convergence failures. Recently, reinforcement-learning-based sequential variable-node (VN) scheduling (RL-S) was shown to improve BP decoding by learning state-dependent update orders. However, the VN-by-VN nature of that approach offers limited within-iteration parallelism, since only one VN is updated at a time. In this paper, we propose a cluster-based extension of RL-S for QLDPC codes. The VNs are partitioned into fixed clusters, and at each scheduling step the RL agent selects one cluster to update, after which all VNs in that cluster are updated in parallel using the same pre-update incoming messages. To keep the tabular state space practical for large cluster sizes, we introduce a permutation-invariant cluster state based on a normalized histogram of local mismatch weights, followed by quantization. This representation makes the number of cluster states depend on the quantization resolution rather than the cluster size. We also develop the corresponding cluster-level Markov decision process, reward function, and Q-learning update. Numerical results on representative QLDPC codes show that the proposed clustered learned scheduling preserves most of the error-rate benefit of VN-level learned sequential scheduling while substantially reducing the number of scheduling decisions per BP iteration, thereby providing an attractive latency-parallelism tradeoff.
summary: This paper introduces a cluster-based extension to Reinforcement Learning (RL) for optimizing Belief Propagation (BP) decoding of QLDPC codes. By allowing the RL agent to select and update entire clusters of nodes in parallel, it significantly reduces the serial scheduling depth compared to node-by-node updates. This achieves an attractive balance between high error correction performance and low computational latency.
main_problem: The performance of Belief-Propagation (BP) decoding for Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check (QLDPC) codes is limited by short cycles and degeneracy, and existing learned scheduling methods suffer from poor within-iteration parallelism.
main_result: The proposed cluster-based RL approach preserves most of the error-rate benefit of fine-grained sequential scheduling while substantially reducing the number of required scheduling decisions per BP iteration, offering a superior latency-parallelism tradeoff.
method: The authors extend Reinforcement Learning (RL) by partitioning Variable Nodes (VNs) into clusters. The RL agent selects an entire cluster to update in parallel, using a quantized, permutation-invariant histogram state representation for the Markov Decision Process.
model_or_system: The work focuses on decoding QLDPC codes used in fault-tolerant quantum computation. Decoding involves message passing over a Tanner graph structure defined by parity-check matrices.
key_observables: Error rate (Block Error Rate/BER) vs. physical error probability ($p_x$), and the number of scheduling decisions required per BP iteration.
important_parameters: Cluster size ($B$), quantization resolution ($L$), and the total iteration budget ($T$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes an ideal parallel cluster-update model for performance gains, and that a quantized state representation is sufficient to capture necessary scheduling information.
figures_summary: Figures compare BER across various decoders (QBP, unclustered RL-S, clustered RL-S) showing that the clustered approach maintains high performance while drastically reducing the required number of scheduling decisions per iteration compared to the unclustered baseline.
paper_structure: The paper first identifies the limitations of standard BP and existing sequential RL methods. It then proposes the cluster-based extension, detailing the state representation (histogram/quantization) and formulating the problem as a cluster-level MDP. Finally, it presents numerical results demonstrating the improved latency-parallelism tradeoff.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses efficiency bottlenecks in quantum error correction decoding by introducing hardware-aware parallelism into an ML-driven scheduling framework, which is highly relevant for implementing fault-tolerant quantum computation protocols.

The proposed quantized clustered RL-S decoder is compared with QBP, QBPGD, and the unclustered RL-S decoder. The RL-S and clustered RL-S decoders use maximum iteration budget T = 100, while QBPGD uses 288 guided-decimation rounds with T = 10 BP iterations per round, i.e., total budget GT = 2880.
